h_watch.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.32 (close watch / seeing not to see)

h_public.left: Hear it from a few people
h_public.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.31 (public / private correction); Pastoral Rule III.7

h_ask.src: Pastoral Rule III.17 (Moses and Hobab: the proud moved by being asked)

ITEMS.stem: A weekend with nothing planned feels…
ITEMS.A: …restless. I’ll have found something to do by noon.
ITEMS.B: …like a gift.
ITEMS.src: Moralia VI.57: the restless "have only the worse labour" at rest

ITEMS.stem: On an ordinary day, your mood is…
ITEMS.A: …on the light side.
ITEMS.B: …on the serious side.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.3: joyful or sad "by temperament"

ITEMS.stem: Before something new and big, you mostly think about…
ITEMS.A: …how well it could go.
ITEMS.B: …what could go wrong.
ITEMS.src: Moralia XXX.51: the fearful "place many things before their eyes"; XXIX.45

ITEMS.stem: In a group, you’re usually…
ITEMS.A: …one of the people doing the talking.
ITEMS.B: …one of the people doing the listening.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.14

ITEMS.stem: Someone is rude to you. In the moment, you…
ITEMS.A: …let them know.
ITEMS.B: …let it go.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.9

ITEMS.stem: Looking back, more of your regrets are about…
ITEMS.A: …things I rushed into.
ITEMS.B: …things I never got round to.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.15: the hasty see afterwards; the slothful put off

ITEMS.stem: You’ve just finished something you worked hard on. Your first thought is…
ITEMS.A: “That’s pretty good.”
ITEMS.B: “It’s not good enough.”
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.8: "singularly eminent" / "exceedingly despised"

ITEMS.stem: When work suddenly piles up, you…
ITEMS.A: …feel buried before I’ve even started.
ITEMS.B: …come alive. I like being busy.
ITEMS.src: Moralia VI.57: the tranquil "give way at the very beginning"

ITEMS.stem: Friends start arguing about something that matters. You…
ITEMS.A: …say where you stand.
ITEMS.B: …try to calm things down.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.22

ITEMS.stem: The music you put on when you’re alone is usually…
ITEMS.A: …slow and a little sad.
ITEMS.B: …upbeat.
ITEMS.src: Moralia XXIX.45: a cheerful or a morose "character"

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I don’t always notice I’ve upset someone until they tell me.
ITEMS.B: One raised eyebrow can stay with me all day.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.7: the impudent "do not know that they are in fault" unless rebuked by many

ITEMS.stem: Which moves you more?
ITEMS.A: The fear of letting people down.
ITEMS.B: The chance to shine.
ITEMS.src: Moralia XXIX.45: the timid "dread punishments"; the proud are "elated with praises"

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I have whole conversations in my head that never happen.
ITEMS.B: I work things out by saying them out loud.
ITEMS.src: Moralia VII.59-60: much talk scatters the mind; over-silence makes "much talking in the heart"

ITEMS.stem: How quickly do you get angry?
ITEMS.A: Fast. It flares up.
ITEMS.B: Slowly. It takes a lot.
ITEMS.src: Moralia V.80

ITEMS.stem: When you see something done badly or unfairly, you…
ITEMS.A: …feel the heat rise.
ITEMS.B: …assume there’s a reason and give people room.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.16

ITEMS.stem: When you’re learning something new, what works better?
ITEMS.A: Explain why it works.
ITEMS.B: Show me someone doing it.
ITEMS.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.30; Pastoral Rule III.6

ITEMS.stem: A friend pulls off something impressive. You feel…
ITEMS.A: …nothing but glad for them.
ITEMS.B: …glad for them, with a little sting.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.10

ITEMS.stem: When you have nothing to do, your thoughts…
ITEMS.A: …get worse. I’m better off busy.
ITEMS.B: …settle. That’s when I think best.
ITEMS.src: Moralia VI.57: "worse tumults of mind" at rest

ITEMS.stem: When you disagree with someone in charge, you…
ITEMS.A: …tell them. Someone has to.
ITEMS.B: …keep it to yourself. It’s not my place.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.17; Moralia XXXIV.51: silent "through fear" thought humility, speech "from the impatience of pride" thought freedom

ITEMS.stem: When something doesn’t get done, it’s usually because…
ITEMS.A: …I never got started.
ITEMS.B: …I started and lost steam.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.34

ITEMS.stem: Which happens to you more?
ITEMS.A: Hours later, I think of what I should have said.
ITEMS.B: I snap, and wish I hadn’t.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.9; Moralia V.79: anger "pent up within the heart from silence"

ITEMS.stem: You’ve made a mistake at work. You…
ITEMS.A: …own it straight away, even if it costs me.
ITEMS.B: …think carefully about how to put it first.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.11 (the urchin rolling up)

ITEMS.stem: A friend asks to borrow money. Your gut says…
ITEMS.A: “Let me think.” I need to know I’ll be okay.
ITEMS.B: “Of course.” I’ll sort out my own needs later.
ITEMS.src: Moralia XV.30: avarice "from apprehension"; Pastoral Rule III.20: over-giving, then want

ITEMS.stem: A decision needs making. You tend to…
ITEMS.A: …wait until you’re sure, sometimes too long.
ITEMS.B: …decide fast and fix it later.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule II.9: "tardiness for the deliberation of seriousness", "precipitate action ... for promptness"

ITEMS.stem: Once you’ve made up your mind, you…
ITEMS.A: …rarely change it.
ITEMS.B: …can be talked out of it fairly easily.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.18

ITEMS.stem: Once you’re angry, how long does it last?
ITEMS.A: A long time. It can last for days.
ITEMS.B: Not long. It’s gone in minutes.
ITEMS.src: Moralia V.80; Cassian Conf. 5.11

ITEMS.stem: Who usually gets the best of you?
ITEMS.A: People I’ve just met.
ITEMS.B: The people I live with.
ITEMS.src: Chrysostom, On the Priesthood III.14 (the athlete at home); Pastoral Rule III.35

ITEMS.stem: You’re asked to take on a big new role. Your first thought is…
ITEMS.A: “I can do that.”
ITEMS.B: “What if I can’t?”
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule I.7 and Nazianzen Or. 2.114: Isaiah volunteers, Jeremiah pleads

ITEMS.stem: What do you need more from the people around you?
ITEMS.A: Someone to slow me down.
ITEMS.B: A push to get going.
ITEMS.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.30

ITEMS.stem: After a hard day, you’re more likely to…
ITEMS.A: …treat yourself. You earned it.
ITEMS.B: …hold back. You don’t want to go soft.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.19

ITEMS.stem: After you’ve done something wrong, you…
ITEMS.A: …feel bad about it for a long time.
ITEMS.B: …fix what you can and move on.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.29-30

ITEMS.stem: When you speak, the words…
ITEMS.A: …come easily.
ITEMS.B: …come hard, even when I know what I mean.
ITEMS.src: Moralia VIII.58

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I’m careful about small things, like being on time and keeping my word.
ITEMS.B: I let small things slide and save my care for big ones.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.33

ITEMS.stem: Which would wear you out faster?
ITEMS.A: A week of back-to-back people and plans.
ITEMS.B: A week at home with nothing to do.
ITEMS.src: Moralia VI.57

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I let things slide that I probably shouldn’t.
ITEMS.B: My anger usually feels justified.
ITEMS.src: Moralia XXXII.45: anger "believed to be" righteous zeal; remissness "regarded as gentleness"

ITEMS.stem: What makes you try harder?
ITEMS.A: Being told I did well.
ITEMS.B: Being told I can do better.
ITEMS.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.31

ITEMS.stem: Which is harder for you?
ITEMS.A: Telling a friend something they won’t want to hear.
ITEMS.B: Letting an argument go when I know I’m right.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.16, III.22

ITEMS.stem: When someone praises your work, you…
ITEMS.A: …think they’re just being kind.
ITEMS.B: …agree, quietly. I know it’s good.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.8

ITEMS.stem: When good news comes, you…
ITEMS.A: …enjoy it straight away.
ITEMS.B: …half wait for the catch.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.3; Moralia XXIX.45

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I’m careful about what I let people see of me.
ITEMS.B: I say what I think, and sometimes at the wrong moment.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.11: the simple must learn "to be silent about what is true"; the insincere guard themselves

ITEMS.stem: Someone needs to point out your mistake. What works better on you?
ITEMS.A: Say it gently. I’ll get it the first time.
ITEMS.B: Say it straight. I can take it.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.7: "hard rebuke" for the impudent, "a modest exhortation" for the bashful

ITEMS.stem: When a friend thinks your plan is a mistake, you…
ITEMS.A: …often end up changing it.
ITEMS.B: …usually go ahead anyway.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.18: the fickle "undervalue" themselves; the obstinate "do not acquiesce in the counsels of others"

ITEMS.stem: When someone is helping you improve, which is better?
ITEMS.A: Pick the one thing that matters most.
ITEMS.B: Point out everything. I’d rather know.
ITEMS.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.32

ITEMS.stem: In a new group, you…
ITEMS.A: …stay near the edge until you’re sure you’re welcome.
ITEMS.B: …find your place in the middle quickly.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.17

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I give on impulse, and sometimes regret it later.
ITEMS.B: I keep a little back, just in case.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.20-21; Cassian Inst. VII.7

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I notice quickly when someone is doing better than me.
ITEMS.B: I admire lots of people I never try to be like.
ITEMS.src: Moralia V.84: we envy only those we think better; Pastoral Rule III.10: "eager backers, but inert spectators"

ITEMS.stem: Which is more true of you?
ITEMS.A: I rarely say anything I haven’t turned over first.
ITEMS.B: I sometimes say things before I’ve really thought them through.
ITEMS.src: Moralia VIII.58, III.23

ITEMS.stem: Which is harder for you?
ITEMS.A: The last ten percent.
ITEMS.B: The first step.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.34

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I don’t much mind what people think, maybe too little.
ITEMS.B: I care what people think of me, maybe too much.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.35; Chrysostom, On the Priesthood V.4

ITEMS.stem: Someone needs to tell you that you got something wrong. What gets through to you?
ITEMS.A: Hearing it from one person, in private.
ITEMS.B: Hearing it from a few people. One person’s opinion I can shrug off.
ITEMS.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.31

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: Most things stay with me for a while.
ITEMS.B: I can laugh off most things.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.3

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I notice when other people overindulge.
ITEMS.B: I enjoy a good meal and don’t think twice about it.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.19: the abstinent tempted to judge "him that eats"

ITEMS.stem: Which is more like you?
ITEMS.A: I stop doing it, but I’m not one for saying sorry.
ITEMS.B: I’m quick to say sorry, and sometimes do it again anyway.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.30: those who lament but do not forsake, and those who forsake but do not lament

ITEMS.stem: When someone wants to change your mind, what works?
ITEMS.A: A strong argument. Win it fairly and I’ll come round.
ITEMS.B: Don’t push. I come round in my own time.
ITEMS.src: Nazianzen Or. 2.32

ITEMS.stem: Your worst mistakes tend to be…
ITEMS.A: …small ones, but they add up.
ITEMS.B: …rare, but big when they come.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.33; Moralia XXXI.87

ITEMS.stem: Which stays with you longer?
ITEMS.A: A criticism.
ITEMS.B: A compliment.
ITEMS.src: Moralia XXIX.45; Chrysostom, On the Priesthood V.4

ITEMS.stem: Someone needs you to do something. Which works better on you?
ITEMS.A: Ask for my help with it.
ITEMS.B: Tell me plainly what to do.
ITEMS.src: Pastoral Rule III.17 (Moses and Hobab)

ITEMS.text: I eat or drink to take the edge off a hard day.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. V; Conf. 5.11, 5.16 (surfeiting and drunkenness)

ITEMS.text: I let my eyes, or my thoughts, linger where they shouldn’t.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. IX.6; Conf. 5.11 (Matthew 5:28)

ITEMS.text: When I have enough, I still find it hard to give some away.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. VII.7, VII.21-22; Moralia XV.30

ITEMS.text: I replay what someone did to me, and what I’d say back.
ITEMS.src: Moralia V.79; Cassian Conf. 5.11 (anger that lasts for days)

ITEMS.text: I like people to know about the good I’ve done.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. XI.3; Pastoral Rule III.35

ITEMS.text: A heaviness comes over me, and even people I love feel like hard work.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. IX.4; Conf. 5.11

ITEMS.text: I find it hard to take correction, even when it’s fair.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. XII.29

ITEMS.text: I can’t settle to what I’m meant to be doing, and I’d rather be anywhere else.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. X.2; Conf. 5.11 (the kind that makes you flee)

ITEMS.text: When I’m lonely or tired, my mind drifts to someone I shouldn’t think about that way.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. IX.6; Moralia XXXI.88

ITEMS.text: I picture people being impressed with me.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. XI.14; Praktikos 13

ITEMS.text: I put off the one thing that matters most.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. X.2-5 (the kind that sends you to sleep)

ITEMS.text: Deep down, I think I’d do most things better than the people around me.
ITEMS.src: Cassian Inst. XII.29; Praktikos 14

ITEMS.stem: Which would you most gladly do for someone this week? Pick up to two.

options.text: Pray for them every day, without telling them.
Have them over and cook them a meal.
Sit with them at the hospital, or through a bad night.
Stand up for them when they’re treated unfairly.
Explain something until they finally understand it.
Quietly pay for something they can’t afford.
Organise the group so no one gets left out.

ITEMS.src: Cassian Conf. 14.4; Budge, Paradise II, no. 605 (Abba Nastir)

ITEMS.stem: What do people usually come to you for? Pick up to two.

options.text: To ask me to pray for them.
A place to stay, or a meal.
Someone to be with them when it’s hard.
Someone to take charge and sort things out.

ITEMS.src: Cassian Conf. 14.5: "the line which he has chosen as the grace which he has received"

ITEMS.stem: Where are you most useful?
ITEMS.A: Out in front, where people can see.
ITEMS.B: Behind the scenes, where nobody notices.
ITEMS.src: Matthew 6:3-4 for the giver; Cassian Conf. 14.4

PRIVATE_NOTE: The next twelve are only for you. Nobody sees these answers, and they never go on your share card. Answer as you really are, not as you would like to be.

hearth.name: The Hearth
hearth.tagline: Light-hearted, and at your best when life is quiet.

spark.name: The Spark
spark.tagline: Light-hearted, and at your best when there is something to do.

deepwell.name: The Deep Well
deepwell.tagline: Serious by nature, and at your best when life is quiet.

forge.name: The Forge
forge.tagline: Serious by nature, and at your best when there is something to do.

stillwater.name: The Still Water
stillwater.tagline: Careful by nature, and at your best when life is quiet.

lookout.name: The Lookout
lookout.tagline: Careful by nature, and at your best when there is something to do.

oak.name: The Oak
oak.tagline: Sure of yourself, and at your best when life is quiet.

herald.name: The Herald
herald.tagline: Sure of yourself, and at your best when there is something to do.

h_show.left: Explain why. I need the reasons.
h_show.right: Show me. Let me see someone do it.
h_show.note: St Gregory the Theologian: "some are led by doctrine, others trained by example"

h_spur.left: Nudge me to get started. I can be slow to begin.
h_spur.right: Slow me down. I run ahead.
h_spur.note: St Gregory the Theologian: "some need the spur, others the curb"

h_praise.left: Tell me what I did well. It makes me try harder.
h_praise.right: Tell me I can do better. I rise to a challenge.
h_praise.note: St Gregory the Theologian: "some are benefited by praise, others by blame"

h_watch.left: Point out everything. I would rather know.
h_watch.right: Pick the one thing that matters most, and let the rest go.
h_watch.note: St Gregory the Theologian: "seeing not to see, and hearing not to hear them"

h_public.left: Tell me if others have noticed it too. One voice I can shrug off.
h_public.note: St Gregory the Theologian: "some, when taken to task in public, others, when privately corrected"

h_win.left: Argue it out with me. Win fairly and I will come round.
h_win.right: Give me time to come round. Pressure makes me dig in.
h_win.note: St Gregory the Theologian: "some it is often more advantageous to conquer — by others to be overcome"

h_ask.left: Tell me plainly what you need.
h_ask.right: Ask for my help. I will give it gladly.
h_ask.note: Gregory the Great: Moses won Hobab over by asking for his help

critic.left: Say it straight. I can take it.
critic.right: Say it gently. A hint is enough.
critic.note: Gregory the Great, on the bold and the bashful

work.left: Be specific about what could be better.
work.right: Start with what I did well.
work.note: Gregory the Great, on the forward and the faint-hearted

talk.left: Give me room to think out loud.
talk.right: Ask what I think. I rarely offer it.
talk.note: Gregory the Great, on the talkative and the silent

nerve.left: Challenge me. I can handle it.
nerve.right: When I get it wrong, tell me what to try next time.
nerve.note: Gregory the Great, on the confident and the faint-hearted
